home.withEnhancementsAndNewFeaturesWhileStayi: with enhancements and new features while staying compatible with the upstream code and plugin ecosystem.
home.openSamandarinCombinesModernFileOperatio: Open Samandarin combines modern file operations, flexible panels, integrated viewers, extensibility, and a stronger configuration and package trust model.

home.catalogEntriesCanProvideTheirOwnIconsPlu: Catalog entries can provide their own icons. Plugin Updates can download and install plugin, runtime, or extension packages automatically, resolve required catalog dependencies, and offer them for installation together.
home.orDirectlyInOpenSamandarinViaThePlugin: or directly in Open Samandarin via the Plugin Updates window in the Samandarin Update Notifier plugin.
home.insteadOfComingFromATraditionalCBackgrou: . Instead of coming from a traditional C++ background, Ondřej is a C# developer and QA test/automation
home.aiSpecialistWhoUsesOpenaiCodexToRapidly: AI specialist who uses OpenAI Codex to rapidly prototype and implement new ideas. The fork exists so AI-written code can evolve separately without risking the quality of the upstream project while development practices mature.
home.theSamandarinNameIsAThreeWayPun: The “Samandarin” name is a three-way pun that pays homage to the Salamander legacy:
home.theBlackAndYellowAmphibianThatInspiredTh: – the black-and-yellow amphibian that inspired the original project.
home.theNaturalToxinSecretedByThatSalamanderS: – the natural toxin secreted by that salamander, symbolising a spicy, daring twist — just like our AI-crafted changes.
home.theVibrantCitrusFruitWithFreshColorPalet: – the vibrant citrus fruit with fresh color palette.
home.togetherTheyPromiseTheSameSalamanderDnaW: Together they promise the same Salamander DNA with a spicy hint of danger.
home.samandarinWritesItsConfigurationToADedic: Samandarin writes its configuration to a dedicated registry hive named "Open Samandarin" to avoid interfering with an official installation. If you previously tried the "tabbed panels PoC" pre-release, manually clean the legacy registry keys because that build still stored settings in the original location.
home.theNameServantSalamanderCameFromABrainst: The name Servant Salamander came from a brainstorming session between Petr Šolín and his friend Pavel Schreib. At the time, the best-known file managers were the aging Norton Commander and the increasingly popular Windows Commander. They wondered why a file manager should be called a commander at all: a good file manager serves its users rather than commands them. That idea led to the name Servant Salamander.
home.theOriginalVersionOfServantSalamanderWas: The original version of Servant Salamander was developed by Petr Šolín while he was studying at the Czech Technical University. He released it as freeware in 1997. After graduating, Petr Šolín founded
home.togetherWithJanRysavyIn2001TheyReleased: together with Jan Ryšavý. In 2001, they released the first shareware version of the program. In 2007, the project was renamed Altap Salamander with the release of version 2.5. Many other programmers and translators have
home.toTheProjectOverTheYearsIn2019: to the project over the years. In 2019, Altap was acquired by
home.afterTheAcquisitionAltapSalamander40Was: . After the acquisition, Altap Salamander 4.0 was released as freeware. In 2023, the source code was released under the GPLv2 license as Open Salamander 5.0.
home.openSamandarinContinuesThisStoryByBlendi: Open Samandarin continues this story by blending the original Salamander DNA with AI-driven enhancements, keeping development moving while inviting adventurous contributors to explore and extend the project.
home.forMakingTheOpenSourceReleaseOfSalamande: for making the open-source release of Salamander possible.
